newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals slightly easier early.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals slightly easier early.

text.p: Precious metals were mostly weaker on Wednesday and the market was eyeing silver for a signal of the market's next move, dealers said.
"We're due for something, and it's probably silver that will do it," a dealer said. Gold and silver have been stuck in narrow price ranges in recent days after last week's push higher.
Bullion fixed at $380.80 an ounce, compared to $381.00 on Tuesday morning and afternoon. Prices barely moved early on, although brisk two-way business was seen.
"There's stuff going on but the books are balanced so you don't see it," a dealer said. "There's a little speculative trade, the buying is short covering and the selling is fresh."

News earlier this week that the Belgian central bank had finished selling its gold reserves had little noticable effect on the market. Analysts had said the news that gold from at least one central bank would no longer enter the marketplace should be reckoned at least mildly bullish.
But several dealers said the market was indifferent because volumes of Belgian sales had never disrupted the market anyway.
"The only thing that's come out of this is a bit of shortcovering by people who thought there was central bank selling a couple of weeks ago -- which was rubbish anyway," one dealer said.
Silver prices were down one cent from Tuesday's London close, at $5.01/$5.03 an ounce. It came off overnight highs around $5.05 an ounce and showed little enthusiasm for a rally.
Prices were expected to hold within its $5.00-$5.10 range, or probe lower to establish a base in the new price band.
"While the platinum group metals are under pressure that stops silver rallying," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were drifting lower, burdened by slack industrial demand and steady producer supply.
Platinum indicated at $383.50/$384.50, was down $1.50 an ounce from Tuesday's London close and was vulnerable towards recent lows around the $380 support level.
Palladium was unchanged at $116.00/$117.00, but looked headed for lower territory, with $115 and then $110 targeted.
